summary.title: Schemas - Schema.org
summary.one_liner: Schema.org's schema overview explains how its type hierarchy, properties, hosted sections (pending, meta, attic) and external extensions are organized for structured data markup.
takeaways: Schema.org is organized as a hierarchy of types, each with associated properties, plus datatypes and enumerations.
Commonly used types include CreativeWork, Event, Organization, Person, Place/LocalBusiness, Product, Review and Action.
Hosted sections such as 'pending' hold terms under discussion and may change; 'meta' is for internal site use; 'attic' holds deprecated terms that should not be used.
External extensions such as GS1 Web Vocabulary and Croissant are independent and not officially approved by the steering group.
Machine-readable files are available in RDF and JSON-LD formats for developers.
summary.summary: This page is the entry point to the schema.org vocabulary documentation. It gives counts of the current vocabulary (826 types, 1540 properties, 19 datatypes, 96 enumerations, 544 enumeration members) and links to commonly used types grouped by area, such as creative works, events, organizations, people, places, products and reviews. It then describes the extension mechanisms: hosted sections (auto, bib, pending, meta), the attic archive for deprecated terms, and a short list of external extensions. The page is reference documentation rather than a tutorial.
